name: Bright Teal
lede: Bright Teal is a near-neon blue-green, recorded almost identically by the ISCC-NBS 1955 dictionary and by Crayola's Sea Green, two sources that rarely describe the same color.

sections.title: An old dictionary, a modern crayon
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS 1955 dictionary places this hue in block 161, a vivid, light green, while Wikipedia's color list separately cites a Crayola crayon called Sea Green at a near-identical value, about 1.3 CIEDE2000 units off [1]. The 2010 xkcd survey independently landed on the same cluster and called it Bright Teal [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[greenish-cyan]], [[light-aquamarine]], [[aquamarine]] and [[light-greenish-blue]], at 4.4, 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4 ΔE [1]. Siblings are [[teal]], [[turquoise]], [[aqua]], and [[mint]], all variations on the same blue-green range [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, has no painting where this near-neon green covers five percent or more of the canvas [2]. The combination of high lightness and very high chroma this hue needs sits well outside what oil paint, once aged and varnished, typically holds [2].
